page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-2 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance configured with 2 vCPUs and 2.0 GB of system memory. It is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 7B13 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The underlying hardware features 1 physical core with 2 threads, supported by 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, and it provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks reveal a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core CPU performance is strong, placing in the top 25% in stress-ng tests, and single-threaded gzip compression performs at an average tier. However, the limited memory capacity of 1.0 GB per core severely constrains multi-core and memory-bound operations. Multi-core stress-ng and Geekbench scores fall into the bottom 10% and 25% respectively. Memory bandwidth is also weak, with large block read-only speeds at 29.49 GB/sec and write speeds at 21.35 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of the n2d-highcpu-2 is its low memory-to-vCPU ratio, which restricts its utility for memory-intensive applications. Database operations, software compilation, and image processing benchmarks all rank in the bottom 10%. Qualitatively, this instance represents a budget-friendly tier for dedicated compute resources, offering high single-thread efficiency without the overhead of excess memory. It is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded CPU tasks, basic text processing, and simple web serving workloads that fit within its 2.0 GB memory envelope.
